Wires inside the cable connect the pins at one end of the cable to the corresponding socket at the other end of the cable. Good wires will measure continuity between the pin and its corresponding socket. Pins should not have continuity between each other.
There may be an exception where one or more pins are tied to ground. If so, wiring diagrams, AS-built drawings, or schematics will identify which pins are grounded.
Wires inside the cable are isolated from the shielding. A good wire does not have continuity between the shielding (wire braiding or foil) and itself.
If the cable is not shielded, the cases of the connectors at each end of the cable DO NOT measure continuity.
If the cable is shielded, the case of the connector has continuity from one end of the cable to the other.

- pins that are recessed making only partial contact.
- scorch (black) marks that may indicate a short, you may smell burned wiring.
- shriveled wire coating or shrink tubing, caused from excessive current.
- wiring that feels hot, it may be hot from excessive current.
- cracked insulation on plugs and jacks.
- dryrot on wiring (insulation becomes brittle and flakes off).
- loose wires going to individual pins and sockets.

LESSON MENU
Let's begin the lesson on BASIC WIRING & CONNECTOR TROUBLESHOOTING THEORY.
Learning to troubleshoot is important to become a good technician. A technician knows how a circuit works and knows how to fix the circuit when it does not work.
Your knowledge of how a good circuit operates will help you identify a circuit that is not operating properly.
Logical troubleshooting takes less time and the results are more predictable.
With the complex circuits in use today, logical troubleshooting procedures must be followed.
As circuits became more complex and were connected over long distances, the trial and error method of troubleshooting required too much time.
When electronic circuits were very simple and contained only a few components, trial and error was an effective troubleshooting technique.
There are two methods to troubleshoot a circuit;
DEFINITION
LOGICAL PROCEDURE - Using a logical process you do Step 1, then Step 2, and so on, until you know what part is bad.
DEFINITION
TRIAL AND ERROR - Using the trial and error method, you replace each part in the circuit until you find the bad part.
There are two methods to troubleshoot a circuit;
You need to learn how to troubleshoot so you can fix circuits that do not operate properly.
Troubleshooting circuits sounds complicated but troubleshooting is nothing more than finding a problem.
